[h1]A decent arena roguelike that is in need of more content. [/h1] Another day another arena roguelike. These things have been a dime a dozen since the success of Vampire Survivors, but Neophyte actually tries to set itself apart rather than trying to ride on VS' coattails. You take a much more active role in Neophyte, moving around a small arena with four spells at your disposal. The game is wave-based with each of three stages having unique enemies and a unique boss. Each time you complete a set of waves, you level up, allowing you to select emblems (power ups), stat boosts and switch out your equipped spells. I haven't counted, but I think it's the fifth set that has the boss fight and once you get through that you move up to the next stage. Beating the game will net you gems that unlock new emblems and spells for you to find in your runs. Now for my actual opinion on the game. Initially I was impressed by the clean visuals, snappy animation and easy to pick up combat. The gameplay is definitely fun and trying out different combinations of spells and emblems is enjoyable. Unfortunately the game really falls down in the overall content department. Yes there are a decent number of spells, and lots of emblems, but the three stages are always the same. Same enemies, same bosses and same small arenas each time you play. It gets pretty dull and the challenge modifiers you unlock make the same content harder, rather than opening up new content. At the end of the day, it's a $3 game and the gameplay is fun so it's not the end of the world, but I would really like to see more content added (alternate stages would be particularly nice). With all that said, if you're a fan of arena roguelikes a la Vampire Survivors, this is definitely one of the better ones and I'd recommend checking it out. **本测评不谈定价以及开发规模等现实因素 2024.1.15更新 去年通关了难度5后（难度6一直没打过去）搁置了，因为觉得太过于随机，纯粹的看运气，以及技能设计也有问题，奥术类技能力压群雄，在高难度中出类拔萃。 去年作者经历了几轮更新，今天重新回来玩了一下，多了几个初始技能，每个元素现在都有2个基础攻击。 玩了几把，有一些不错的点子，但之前劝退我的点仍然没有解决，且仍是游戏目前最大的缺点。 1、在高难度下，奥术类技能仍然是出类拔萃，尤其是奥术环刃，就冲它可以摧毁敌人远程飞行物的特点就可以永远占据T0。其他的例如火焰手里剑，闪电箭，火焰柱，在高难度下的操作难度都很大，操作空间也很小。 2、游戏的选技能过于随机，高难度在第一关BOSS前如果没有Roll到好的技能基本GG。 3、游戏的选技能策略固定，不缺伤害，缺辅助技能，同2，如果前期没有Roll到比较好的恢复技能，例如杀敌回蓝，掉落更多血瓶，血瓶回蓝，这3可以说是大部分肉搏bd的标配，在第一关BOSS前没有Roll到其中2个，也基本GG。 目前仍然是不推荐。 —————————————————————— 这是一个纯Rogue类游戏，每局游玩时间在25-30min之间（难度6）。 不是刷刷刷类型，并非吸血鬼这类游戏，没有其他游戏所谓的BD，所有的升级都是为了让你的技能放得更多（续航）、更痛（伤害）。技能本身的形态是不会改变的。 所有的升级选项都是随机出现，虽然给了刷新选项的功能，但是你这个刷新凭什么又让我刷到我不想要的东西？ 做了12个人物数值来稀释成长的上限，这个倒没啥。 总而言之我不推荐来这个游戏浪费时间，你只要玩过一把你就相当于玩完了这个游戏的所有内容，后面只是时间和概率的问题。

A title I picked up in the days of Roguelike craze, and while not all games were gems, this gem is certainly a game. Cute, sweet, and simple in it's execution, the runs offer enough variety and challenge when paired with the simple style that creates some fun runs. The skills are varied and creative, with interesting upgrades and synergies between spells and passive runes, creating hectic combinations with fun mage power fantasies. The enemies are definitely a highlight, as their designs are all cute and clear while providing a great variety of mechanics to play around. Paired with simple yet effective skills, the game remains readable even in the more hectic Roguelike moments, thanks to Neophyte's cute and simple style. All of this works even better when the catchy tracks are bumping. While not the best representation of Early Access on Steam, Neophyte is also a reminder that everyone behind the screens is human, and I sincerely hope Regal Pigeon all the best in life. Thank you for sharing a part of yourself, I certainly have no regrets supporting you and your game.

Neophyte is a compact action roguelike that thrives on speed, experimentation, and magical chaos. Instead of building itself around a heavy storyline or complicated progression systems, the game focuses entirely on delivering fast-paced combat where players gradually evolve into devastating spellcasters capable of wiping entire arenas clean. Its structure is straightforward, but that simplicity works in its favor because nearly every mechanic feeds directly into the addictive combat loop. From the opening moments, the game pushes players into hectic battles against waves of enemies while encouraging constant movement, quick decision-making, and creative spell combinations. The core gameplay revolves around building a personalized arsenal of magical abilities during each run. Players can equip different spells and combine them into highly destructive setups that dramatically change how encounters play out. Some builds focus on aggressive close-range attacks with spinning blades or explosive shockwaves, while others lean toward long-distance destruction through beams, projectiles, and elemental attacks. What makes the system satisfying is how quickly builds can become overwhelmingly powerful. The game embraces the fantasy of becoming an unstoppable wizard, and it rarely holds back when rewarding players with absurdly effective combinations. Combat is the strongest aspect of the experience. Battles are frantic, responsive, and filled with nonstop action. Enemy groups quickly surround the player, forcing careful positioning and constant movement while spells explode across the screen in every direction. The controls feel fluid enough to support the game’s high-speed pacing, and the steady stream of upgrades keeps each run engaging from beginning to end. Even failed attempts remain entertaining because experimenting with new spell synergies is enjoyable on its own. The game understands the appeal of roguelikes built around replayability, and it consistently encourages players to dive back in for another run. Visually, Neophyte adopts a simple but colorful presentation style that prioritizes readability and action. The environments themselves are relatively minimalistic, but the spell effects help create a strong visual identity. Bright magical attacks, swirling projectiles, and explosive bursts constantly fill the battlefield, giving combat a satisfying sense of impact. The visual effects make every build feel powerful, especially during later stages when the screen becomes crowded with enemies and magical attacks. While the graphics are not especially detailed, they fit the arcade-style gameplay perfectly and help maintain the game’s energetic pace. One of the game’s biggest strengths is its accessibility. Neophyte avoids overwhelming players with unnecessary complexity, making it easy for newcomers to understand while still leaving enough room for experienced roguelike fans to experiment with advanced builds. Runs are relatively short and densely packed with action, making the game ideal for quick sessions without sacrificing replay value. The progression systems outside combat are intentionally lightweight, allowing players to focus more on gameplay experimentation rather than managing complicated mechanics between runs. The pacing also deserves praise because the game wastes very little time. Upgrades appear frequently, combat encounters arrive quickly, and the action rarely slows down long enough to become dull. This structure gives Neophyte an almost arcade-like rhythm where each session feels compact but rewarding. There is a constant sense of momentum as players grow stronger, discover new abilities, and attempt increasingly dangerous encounters. That progression curve creates the satisfying feeling of gradually turning from a vulnerable spellcaster into a walking catastrophe capable of clearing entire enemy waves within seconds. Despite its strengths, the game does have limitations that become more noticeable during extended play sessions. The overall content variety can feel somewhat limited compared to larger roguelikes in the genre. Players looking for deep narrative elements, massive progression trees, or highly varied environments may eventually find the experience repetitive. While the spell system provides strong replayability, the arena-focused structure and recurring enemy patterns can occasionally make runs feel familiar after many hours. Another issue comes from the sheer amount of visual chaos during intense battles. Some spell combinations create such overwhelming effects that enemy attacks can become difficult to track. Although the game remains playable even during these moments, the clutter occasionally affects visibility and precision. Fortunately, the responsive controls and fast movement help offset most of these frustrations. What ultimately makes Neophyte stand out is its commitment to pure gameplay satisfaction. The game knows exactly what it wants to deliver and stays focused on that goal from start to finish. It captures the excitement of building outrageously powerful magical combinations without burying players under unnecessary systems or excessive downtime. Every mechanic exists to support the central fantasy of becoming a destructive wizard surviving impossible odds through clever spell usage and rapid adaptation. Neophyte may not redefine the roguelike genre, but it succeeds as a highly entertaining and focused action experience. Its fast combat, rewarding progression, and satisfying spell experimentation make it an easy recommendation for fans of arcade-style roguelikes and magic-heavy action games. The streamlined design and energetic pacing help it stand out among many smaller indie releases, offering a gameplay loop that remains fun long after the first few runs. Rating: 8/10

For under $5, you have a solid arcade style game you can pick up and play with lots of different spells and passives. There are also scaling difficulties to it, enemy variants and 3 playable characters that are fun in their own ways. There is enough game in it for me to put 24 hours of my life into it and I still pop in once in a while to play a run or two and again its 5 frigging dollars. I could understand the criticisms if it was an expensive game that wasn't anywhere near finished, but Neophyte as it stands has a complete game in it. Sure it could have more content, but there is plenty packed into the price tag and pretty much every game could have more content. Some of you people need to be realistic, learn some empathy and grow up. When your whole life gets completely turned upside down abruptly and drastically, I would love to see how you continue to do your passion projects and manage yourselves.

Neophyte is a game where you use your collection of abilities and buffs to cull a horde of dudes. It's not an interesting premise, but it's one of my favorite games due to how engaging it is at all times. The requirements to beat Neophyte can split up into two key skills; build-making and split-second decision making. Making a good build and understand how to play it is important to clearing out enemies efficiently, and being comfortable with the game's base mechanics (knowing when to dash, when to use defensive spells, etc) is important to surviving short bursts of intense damage. But the critical thing to understand is that your decision making cannot fully make up for your poor build-making, and vice versa. If there are too many enemies, it doesn't matter how good you are at the game, you'll still die. If you're taking a lot of damage, it doesn't matter how good your build is, you'll still die. This is ultimately why I keep coming back to Neophyte, because it doesn't let me automatically win even if I get an incredibly powerful build, or if I get good enough at the base mechanics with a subpar build. I'm still liable to take massive damage if I don't take the right precautions, and there's still interesting decisions to be made in my builds. The abilities never read as "crazy," but they're valuable puzzle pieces that you can choose to add to your build, and they're consistent, too. There can be a spell in your arsenal that has no synergy with the rest of your collection, but is still important because it plays a valuable role in your gameplan. This is the principle that I think makes games like Slay the Spire phenomenal; not forcing the player to make a "burn" build, or a "attack speed" build. These games punish you for thinking in that simple manner, and I really enjoy it. This game hasn't been updated in a while, and the developer has stated that there aren't any more updates planned. But like....this game has a lot of content for only costing $3. I've seen many games cost $15-20 and have half of this game's content. If you end up loving the game like I do, this is a complete no-brainer of a purchase. The question is just whether you think you'd enjoy the game as much as I do, and I hope my review has given you an idea of how you'd answer that.
